problems.title: Higher-order safety theorem omits required initial barrier-domain conditions
source_locations: PDF pp.13-14 AppendixB, especially initialization after Eq.(22)
problems.original_claim: Initial b_j>=0 alone suffices for safety of ABNet for all later times.
problems.suspect_step: Positive derivative initialization is used to infer nonnegative higher-order barrier state without initial membership.
assumptions_verified: QP feasible everywhere, exact locally Lipschitz feedback
problems.decisive_evidence: Even granting exact/sign-corrected QP, q1=-t exp(-t), v1=(t-1)exp(-t), u1=(2-t)exp(-t) for0<t<1 satisfies constraint at equality and is QP minimum, yet q1<0. psi11=-exp(-t)<0 while its derivative is positive. At boundary no finite penalty can fix psi11(0)=-1.
counterevidence: Correct HOCBF theorem on all initial psi_j,i>=0 excludes witness.
problems.core_dependency: Independent invalid step in central safety theorem and its cited merging proof, even after fixing P1.

repair.proposal: Require all initial psi_j,i>=0 plus feasibility/regularity and account for resets/time variation.
repair.verified_scope: Integrating-factor proof for constant unit-linear second-order barriers and shared-constraint mixtures.
repair.author_adoption: Unknown; no author contact or revised theorem supplied.
